title: The Man Who Mailed Himself in a Wooden Crate Across the World
sources: BBC News / Brian Robson 'The Crate Escape' (1965) - 19-year-old Welshman Brian Robson shipped himself from Melbourne to London as air freight inside a small wooden crate.
Los Angeles Times Archives (April 1965) - Robson survived 96 hours trapped in airline cargo holds, accidentally arriving in Los Angeles where customs officials found him alive.

lines.text: In nineteen sixty five, a broke teenager nailed himself inside a tiny wooden crate -
lines.caps: In 1965, | a broke teenager | nailed himself | inside a wooden crate -

lines.text: and mailed himself halfway across the world as air cargo.
Nineteen year old Brian Robson was stranded in Australia, desperately homesick for the United Kingdom.
An airline ticket cost seven hundred pounds, but Brian had almost nothing.
So he bought a wooden mini-crate, packed a pillow, a flashlight, and a hammer,
and had two friends nail the wooden lid shut over his head.
They stamped This Side Up on the crate and checked him into air freight, expecting a thirty-six hour flight.
Instead, careless airport baggage handlers loaded the box completely upside down!
For four agonizing days, blood rushed to his head in freezing cargo holds as he drifted in and out of consciousness.
Even worse, the flight was rerouted, dumping the crate in a Los Angeles warehouse.
A customs inspector spotted a small hole, peeked inside, and saw two human eyes blinking in the dark.
He screamed, thinking he had seen a ghost!
Paramedics broke the crate open, saving Brian from severe dehydration after ninety-six hours in the mail.
